To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrochemical behavior of diazophenyloxycarbonylcalix[4]-arene is sensitive toward divalent cations and that the electrochemical signals are different for different divalent cations, and the electrochemical behavior is not sensitive toward monovalent alkalis.

the electrochemical properties of o-CAC ando-EAC are sensitive to divalent metal ions. o-CAC preferential bindswith alkaline earth and some transition metal ions, while no significant changes in the voltammetric signals were observed in o-EC with alkaline earth metals.

the voltammetric changes of diazo-phenylcalix[ 4]arenes in the presence of alkaline earth and other transition metal ions are attributed to the complexation of the diazo-phenyloxy groups with metal ions, and the voltammetric change of o-CAC is much more significant than that of o-EAC, which is attributed to the complex formation with the metal ion.

the development of new electrochemical methods for cation recognition with diazophenol-calixarenes and the electrochemistry of the diazophenyloxazolinecalix[4]-arenes.
the development of electrochemical sensors based on diazophenolcalix[4]-arenes.
the electrochemical studies of diazophenoxyazocalix[arenes] for the cation recognition.

diazo-coupled calix[4]ares are useful electrochemical probes for the detection of metal ions in solution.
the electrochemical behavior is a useful tool to evaluate the metal ion complexation ability and selectivity in the diazocalix[4]-arene derivatives.
o-CAC is a suitable candidate as an anion receptor for divalent anion, whereas o-EAC is a suitable receptor for divalent transition metal ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
o-EAC can be used as a selective sensor for transition metals and o-CAC can be used for alkaline earth metals.
the electrochemical properties of the diazophenyldioxocalix[4]-arenes are sensitive to divalent metal ions.
the electrochemical method is useful to evaluate the complexation behavior of diazo-calix[4]arenas toward metal ions.

the electrochemistry of diazophenylo-calixarenes is very useful for the study of their cation complexation properties.
the diazophenyloxycalix[4]arenecarboxylic acids can be used as electrochemical probes for metal cation recognition.
the voltammetric response of diazophenyloxacalix[4] arenes toward metal ions is highly dependent on the nature of the substituent group on the diazophenyloxy group.
